notas:
How I chose what to keep: in each study I kept the most comprehensive non-overlapping set (the whole period, or one row per independent campaign) and dropped the sub-periods, monthly or seasonal parts, pooled re-aggregations, duplicate panels and conditional re-analyses. I applied the same rule within each study. Where two versions of the same annual S existed, I kept the one computed as a ratio of totals (1 - sum Ec / sum Eo) and dropped the unweighted mean of monthly rates (Huang2023, S2026).

Judgement calls you may want to override:
(1) H2001 Nymphaea: I kept the whole-experiment row 6. Rows 4-5 report different phi (21% vs 18%), so you could keep those two instead and drop row 6.
(2) Rahman2024: rows 1-3 split one condition by time of day. I kept the 12 pm row. A better fix is one pooled row weighted by open-water evaporation (Eo): about 0.26, using 0.081, 0.39 and 0.24 cm/h.
(3) S2018 rows 13-18 and Duan2026 row 5: I excluded them even though their phi differs, because they are linear area scalings of another row (S proportional to phi by construction), not separate measurements.
(4) S2026: I kept the annual statistical year (rows 14-15) instead of the 13-month headline (rows 1-2). The hexagonal-float row 3 (Apr-Sep only) is kept as an independent cover.

Kept on purpose (all independent):
- Albalasmeh rows 19-25: model runs for a different site (GhM).
- Aminzadeh rows 9-10: 3 m depth scenario.
- Duan rows 6-8: a different pond, and the non-overlapping 2025 months.
- Ilgen: all rows (different lakes, phi and future periods). Rows 4-6 are threshold-derived points.
- JC2023: campaigns 1 and 2 are non-overlapping.
- Mady rows 1-16 (season x year campaigns), sphere rows 18-20, and partial-cover rows 21 and 23.
- Cooley 1970: all periods are non-overlapping.
- Wang rows 11-15: reservoir fence test. These are computed from still-water rates, so they are not fully independent of the dropped rows 6-10, but they come from a different site and phi.
- Yadima2020: monthly rows only, with no aggregate available.

Not excluded, but worth flagging:
- B2026 rows 1-4 all have S/phi = 0.224 exactly (linear model construction), so together they carry one piece of information. Consider down-weighting them.
- Cross-study overlaps fall outside this per-study task:
  - Aminzadeh2018 lab rows 1-6 versus Lehmann2019 rows 22-24 (same ETH 0.20 m disc lab setup).
  - Raksaksri2023 versus Benjaoran2023 (same ponds).
  - JC2023 versus de2023 (same site, different periods).
  - Assouline2011 equations versus the Assouline2010 data.
  - Mady2021 has two text versions: the paper and the ETH thesis.
